sections.h2: How does property tax work in Mercer County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
Three offices on West Lexington Street in Harrodsburg handle Mercer County tax. The PVA appraises each parcel, the sheriff takes the money, and the county clerk records liens and picks up any bill still open once April 15 passes.

By the sheriff's own account the office collects more than $8,000,000 a year, so tax is a big share of its workload. Houses inside Harrodsburg also get a city bill, explained below.

sections.h2: What is Mercer County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Mercer sits in the Bluegrass of central Kentucky on roughly 249 square miles of land. Lincoln County, Virginia gave up the territory in 1785, and the new county took the name of General Hugh Mercer. Harrodsburg, the seat, was the first city formally chartered in what was then Kentucky County, according to Wikipedia. Burgin is the second city, and Salvisa is a census designated place.

Visitors come for Old Fort Harrod State Park, the Shaker Village of Pleasant Hill with its 30 or more historic buildings, and Herrington Lake. The Louisville Southern Railroad reached Harrodsburg in 1888. Neighbors are Anderson, Woodford, Jessamine, Garrard, Boyle and Washington counties.

The Census Bureau lists 132 building permits for Mercer County in 2025, so some buyers will compare an older house with a new build.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about housing in Mercer County?
sections.html:
The 2020 count came to 22,641 people, up from 21,331 in 2010, and the mid-2025 estimate stands at 23,733. Housing units number 10,824.

The 2020 through 2024 survey adds:

  • Owner occupancy is 75.9 percent.
  • Monthly owner costs have a median of $1,373 with a mortgage and $497 without.
  • 86.8 percent of households subscribe to broadband.
  • The average commute is 27.2 minutes.
  • Density is 90.9 people per square mile, well above the 30.0 to 35.5 seen in Menifee and Metcalfe.

sections.h2: Which Mercer County offices should you contact?
sections.html:
Contact details from the county pages and the PVA site:

  • Sheriff: bills and payments, in person at 207 W. Lexington St. or by mail to P.O. Box 126, Harrodsburg, KY 40330. Phone (859) 734-4221. The office keeps weekday hours of 8:00 to 4:30 and has a drop box out front for evenings and weekends.
  • PVA: appraisals and exemption forms. Same street address, P.O. Box 244, phone (859) 734-6330, same weekday schedule.
  • County Clerk: deeds, liens and delinquent bills. Courthouse address, P.O. Box 426, phone (859) 734-6310.

The PVA site has a public property search with limited detail, and a paid subscription opens the full database.

sections.h2: Why do Harrodsburg homeowners get two tax bills?
sections.html:
A house within Harrodsburg pays two governments. The city sends its own bill, and the county sheriff bundles the county, state, library, extension, soil conservation, health and school taxes. City Hall says mailings go out at the end of September.

For 2025 the city lists these rates per $100 of assessed value:

  • City of Harrodsburg: 0.063
  • Kentucky state: 0.106
  • Mercer County: 0.116
  • Library: 0.064
  • Extension office: 0.042
  • Soil conservation: 0.010
  • Health department: 0.050
  • Mercer County schools: 0.705

The city's own example turns a $200,000 assessment into $126 of city tax. Rates are reviewed each year, so use the rate on your current bill.

sections.h2: What are the Mercer County tax due dates?
sections.html:
The sheriff's page lays out this calendar for 2026 bills. It mirrors KRS 134.015, with the county's own wording for the later penalty.

  • Oct. 1 through Nov. 1, 2026: discount of 2 percent.
  • Nov. 2 through Dec. 31, 2026: the amount printed.
  • January 2027: a 5 percent penalty.
  • Later: a 10 percent penalty, with a further 10 percent sheriff fee on payments made between Feb. 1 and April 15.

Whatever is still open moves to the county clerk when business closes on April 15, 2027. The sheriff asks anyone who gets no bill to phone the office. Bills arrive on a white postcard with a yellow strip, which is easy to mistake for junk mail.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a Mercer County assessment?
sections.html:
Ask for a PVA conference during the inspection window, a 13 day stretch that starts the first Monday of May. A conference that ends in disagreement leads to a filing at the county clerk's office, where you state your own figure.

A three person board takes appeals 25 to 35 days after the window, starting with a look at recent sales of comparable homes. If you hire someone to speak for you, KRS 133.120 limits the choice to lawyers, CPAs, licensed brokers or appraisers and similar professionals, plus your own employees, and that person needs your written authorization.

Mercer County mixes town lots, farms and acreage on one roll, so choose sales of homes like yours. A farm house on acreage and a town lot do not compare well.

sections.h2: Who can claim the homestead exemption in Mercer County?
sections.html:
People 65 or older, and people classified as totally disabled, can claim it on their own residence. The sheriff's page tells them to call the PVA at (859) 734-6330 if they have not signed up.

Under KRS 132.810 a residential unit gets one exemption, and a mobile home counts as a unit. The value you write on the application cannot be used to raise your assessment. Disabled owners under 65 reapply yearly, except service connected totally disabled veterans and people found permanently disabled under Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems rules.

sections.h2: What happens if Mercer County tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
After April 15 the clerk issues a certificate of delinquency, and a lien attaches to the property. Interest accrues at 1 percent a month, and fees of 10 percent for the clerk and 20 percent for the county attorney follow. A $1,000 bill in the state's worked example becomes $1,254 at transfer and about $1,611 after the first attorney notice.

Certificates may be sold to outside buyers starting in mid-July. A sold certificate means dealing with that buyer, who may add fees. Payment plans come through the county attorney before a sale.

sections.h2: What should a Mercer County seller know about the January 1 rule?
sections.html:
January 1 fixes tax ownership. The Mercer County PVA explains that a buyer who closes later in the year still sees the bill issued to the former owner until the next calendar year, although the office tries to mail the new owner a copy using the recorded deed.

That shapes every closing. A buyer who never gets the bill can ask the sheriff for it, and the contract should say who covers that year's tax. If an older bill sits at the clerk, request a payoff figure before choosing a closing date.

faqs.q: Where do I pay my Mercer County property tax bill?
faqs.a: Pay the Mercer County Sheriff at 207 W. Lexington St. in Harrodsburg, or mail it to P.O. Box 126. A drop box on the front of the building takes payments after hours.

faqs.q: Does the sheriff collect the Harrodsburg city tax too?
faqs.a: No. The city sends its own bill, and the county sheriff sends a separate one for county, state and school taxes.

faqs.q: When does the 2 percent discount end in Mercer County?
faqs.a: The 2026 discount runs from October 1 through November 1, 2026. Payment at face value is accepted from November 2 through December 31.

faqs.q: Can I get a refund of the homestead exemption if I applied late?
faqs.a: Yes. Under KRS 132.810, a person who qualifies after paying receives a refund of the tax on the exempt amount.

faqs.q: I bought a house after January 1. Who gets the bill?
faqs.a: The bill is issued in the former owner's name until the next calendar year. The new owner can contact the sheriff at (859) 734-4221 for a copy.
